These pieces are very much meant to work in concert with like pieces. Rooks connect, pawns form pawn lines, unlike knights and bishops which quite often don't necessarily need to work with their counterparts. So I think it makes more sense to score pawns and rooks on a curve. First rook could be worth 6 points, second rook could be worth 4 points, for example. You still lose 10 points in total when you lose them both, but losing the first one hurts more than losing the second. They're also really hard to move during the early game so maybe that's something that should be accounted for too.

It seems to me that whoever made the scoring system for chess way oversimplified it for a game that is this in-depth with strategy.
I think rooks and maybe pawns should be scored differently.
